messages:
nina: Quick sync — landed a lightweight two-stage speculative flow on the 12B quant build this morning. Results are surprising: 2.6x tail QPS improvement on our demo workload with <10ms median added overhead.

drew: nice. is that with lazy-kv enabled?

nina: yes, lazy-kv + early-prob cutoff (threshold 0.82). kept beam/sample configs the same.

sam: can you paste the perf numbers and the eval diffs?

nina: pasted below. short summary first: throughput up, latency p95 down ~35%, but measured slight BLEU drop on the summarization holdout (~0.7 pts) and a 1.1% increase in factuality-flag rate for the safety suite.

maya: when you say "early-prob cutoff" — is that per-token or per-block?

nina: per-token score at generation step. heuristic: if top token prob / runner-up > cutoff we skip speculative rescore and accept fast-path.

drew: interesting — reminds me of the bandit threshold paper. did you tune cutoff on validation or pick heuristically?

nina: tuned on a 2k prompt val split. swept [0.7,0.75,0.8,0.82,0.85]. 0.82 was best throughput/quality balance.

sam: paste from the smoke run?

nina: here are snippets from the smoke run (raw):

```
model: redwood-12b-q4_2
setup: lazy-kv=true, speculative=two-stage-lite, cutoff=0.82
workload: summarize-1000 (mean len 320 tokens)
baseline QPS: 18.3
speculative QPS: 49.1
median latency baseline: 84ms
median latency speculative: 72ms
p95 baseline: 410ms
p95 speculative: 270ms
BLEU-summary baseline: 29.4
BLEU-summary speculative: 28.7
factual-flag rate baseline: 3.2%
factual-flag rate speculative: 4.3%
```

maya: wow that QPS jump is solid. the BLEU dip isn't tiny though. do we have examples where it regressed?

nina: yes, I pulled a few failure cases — typically hallucinated location/entity swaps when the model used a shorter path earlier. putting a tiny rerank (single-sample) on flagged prompts catches most.

drew: what's the extra cost of that rerank? does it kill the gains?

nina: measured an adaptive rerank policy: only rerank if ngram overlap below 0.6 or the speculative path had entropy < 1.2. this keeps rerank rate ~12% and end-to-end QPS stays ~38 (still 2.1x baseline).

sam: did you run the eval suite for safety & instruction-following? numbers?

nina: quick smoke: instruction compliance delta -0.4%, refusal rate unchanged. safety classifier flags up 1.1% overall (total from earlier). detailed logs uploaded to the run bucket (s3://redwood-test/runs/2927601111/).

ml-bot: perf-check: all pods healthy, no OOMs. cpu infra cost delta: +6% (more headroom), gpu time per token -42%.

maya: curious about interaction with quant noise — q4_2 sometimes increases greedy peak probs. could that bias cutoff decisions?

nina: noted. I ran the same sweep on float16 bench and saw cutoff optimal at 0.78 there. quant is indeed shifting the calibration.

drew: so this implies we need cutoffs per model/quant pair. can we auto-calibrate during canary?

nina: proto idea: run a 500-prompt calibration job that outputs token-level calibration stats, pick cutoff minimizing expected loss = alpha * (regression_rate) + beta * (1/throughput). alpha/beta tunable.

sam: we should also bake a conservative fallback: if rerank rate > 25% or factual-flag spikes > 2x baseline, disable speculative path automatically.

nina: agree. added to rollout checklist.

ops-bot: deploy logs: canary deployed to us-west-2 (8 pods). Canary started at 2927601140.

maya: what's the plan for a proper eval run? i want a holdout that includes long context Qs and instruction heavy tasks.

nina: proposed eval matrix: (1) summarization holdout 5k, (2) longchat 2k (mean 4k ctx), (3) instruction suite 3k, (4) safety holdout 4k. run each on float16 and q4_2 across cutoffs [0.75,0.78,0.82].

drew: timeline?

nina: scheduling a full run tomorrow AM. estimated 6h per config. starting with q4_2 since it's the most urgent.

sam: please capture per-prompt meta: rerank_decision, top1_prob, delta_entropy. that will help build a tiny ML classifier later.

nina: yup capturing those fields. also included `fast_path_taken` boolean.

ml-bot: eval-run queued: job-id 202603-292760. estimated completion 2927685000.

maya: last ask — add a small human eval batch (200 examples) for high-impact customers to sanity check quality changes.

nina: added. tagging @solutions for the customer panel. will push results to the PR and chart diffs in console. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks — this feels promising. keep notes of any calibration drift post-deploy.

nina: will do. closing for now unless someone else wants to add quick checks.
